concepts.label: Arm signals for turning and stopping
concepts.statement: Arm pointing down means slow or stop, arm pointing up means right turn, and arm straight out means left turn.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: ARM POINTING DOWN ARM POINTING UP ARM STRAIGHT OUT

questions.question: A driver extends their left arm straight out of the window. What are they signalling?
choices: That they are slowing or stopping
That it is safe to pass them
questions.explanation: Arm straight out means a left turn. The handbook shows three arm signals side by side: arm pointing down for slow or stop, arm pointing up for a right turn, and arm straight out for a left turn. These matter when turn signals fail, and for cyclists.

questions.question: Which arm signal means the driver is about to make a right turn?
questions.explanation: Arm pointing up signals a right turn. It is easy to confuse with arm straight out, which is a left turn — the bent, upward arm is the one that means right.

questions.question: You are following a car whose driver puts an arm out of the window pointing down toward the road. What should you expect?
choices: The car is about to slow down or stop
The car is about to turn left
The car is about to turn right
The driver is signalling for you to overtake
questions.explanation: Arm pointing down means slow or stop. Treat it exactly as you would brake lights — increase your following distance and prepare to stop, since the driver may be signalling by arm precisely because their lights are not working.

questions.question: Which pairing of arm signal to meaning is NOT correct?
choices: Arm straight out means slow or stop
Arm pointing down means slow or stop
Arm pointing up means right turn
Arm straight out means left turn
questions.explanation: Arm straight out means a left turn, not slow or stop. Slow or stop is signalled with the arm pointing down. The other three pairings are exactly as the handbook shows them.
